title: Project Mclaren - Capital A x Market Performance Group

sentences.text: Foreign.
Hey John, how you doing?
Good.
Hey Andrew, how are you?
Yeah, I'm good, thank you.
I'm good.
Whereabouts are you in New York today?
I'm actually in New Jersey at the moment.
I live in Arizona in the States half the year and then I live in New Jersey half the year to you.
Oh wow.
Well, you're chasing the sun.
Yeah.
Or trying to get out of the sun in the Arizona in the heat of the summer and come to the beach in the, in the summertime.
So yeah, brilliant.
Okay.
Living the dream.
I'm basically chasing my grandchildren so I'm chasing that.
That's it.
Three, three in Jersey and two in Arizona, so.
Oh wow.
We kind of follow our kids a little bit.
Yeah.
Well, congratulations.
It sounds like you got life supported.
Thanks for meeting with us today.
I think the main thing really is just that we like to introduce ourselves first before prospects to the clients.
If we haven't met before.
It's always good to just have a quick conversation, make sure you're a real person, 100% right.
So I got a note, solicited email, it was a little intriguing so I, I picked it up.
Hey, you want me to go, you want me to go first and then.
Well, I'm happy to tell you a little bit about us first, John.
So we're capital A.
We're Capital A.
We're based in the UK but actually the majority of our work is US based and we're an M and A advisory.
We work exclusively in marketing services.
So all of our clients are either marketing agencies or buyers of marketing agencies.

So on the buy side we directly work with pro private equity or private investors as well and we help them to find the types of targets they want to acquire and help the entire process on the buy side as well.
So our sell side platform is Agencies co, which you may have already seen the listing on.
So that's our marketplace for agency owners to buy and sell as well.
So yeah, good to see you.
I can see you are real now.
Although it could be AI you never know nowadays.
Yeah, you never know.
So if there's any sort of preliminary questions then obviously I can, I can help you with those to some degree.
But happy to give you sort of the big, the big picture as well with tsg.
It'd be great to hear a little bit about you guys.
I don't believe we've come across you before.
So yeah, we're a Omni based channel, basically service consumer package.
Good companies across, primarily US based, both small mid to large tier companies.

We have A services agency that basically services every brick and mortar in the US we build teams around each one of those channels, we call them verticals and we kind of run that business separately.
And then we have a rather large digital e commerce presence.
We've been in business for about 25 years.
Started out kind of as a consulting company.
We still have a consulting practice providing consulting services for sales and marketing for consumer packaged good companies.
But we grew that business from about 9 million in 2015 to today we're about $225 million.
We've hit two exits.
We exited in 20 to a private equity company.
We rolled over 35%, stayed involved as a management team.
They had a three year exit.
We had grown our business from about 50, 60 million when they bought it to that 220 million dollar number we just exited in 24 to Sentinel Capital.
Sentinel is a, you know, pretty large private equity firm based out of New York.
They own roughly 65 to 70% of the business.
Again, management rolled over again into the business.
Still running the business today.
My background, I spent 35 years with Johnson and Johnson.
I decided I was going to retire.
Failed miserably at that.
Joined MPG in 2015, spent 10 years there kind of serving as their chief operating officer.
I then moved to a board position in this new Sentinel Capital ownership structure.
And I do M and A form.
We completed the transaction January of 24.
We've done four deals, soon to be five.
So we're doing some bolt on activity that makes strategic sense for us to either build out capability or add capability, but all centered around the same thing.
You know, basically a omnichannel organization that serves consumer packaged goods.
We're primarily beauty and healthcare and personal.
But we've got a pretty growing food business.
So we're a little agnostic to food.
We just made an acquisition this past year, got into the do it yourself category.
So we're strong both in an independent retailer as well as, you know, the big box store, Home Depot, Lowe's and acquired a business that did roughly $35 million of revenue.
You know, so it added some critical mass to everybody getting that space.
And we're starting to take a look at pet.
You know, it's kind of a rounding out and we've been thinking about opportunities.
We've got a small business in Canada, but it's, it's our first entree outside the US based organization.
We're about 700 people.
If today's conversation made sense for both of us.
There's four or five people I'd want to get involved, you know, in a conversation, share the deck with and, you know, see if it took us anywhere.
Yeah, okay.
Brilliant.
Well, yeah, great fit.
Obviously, I'm really impressed with your track record.
That's quite a thing.
So you've been through two private equity deals already, which is fantastic experience, isn't it?
Yeah, I think we've had, you know, I'd have to go back and count, to be fair.
We were 11.
We've probably had 14 or 15 bolt on acquisitions over the course of eight or nine years.
Yeah.
Wow.
Fantastic.
I do a podcast about this sort of thing.
I think you'd be a really good guest.
Actually set that one up.
Okay, cool.
So what can I tell you about these guys?
Well, they are obviously in the retail space.
The sort of shopper media thing is still quite a growing market, I think, both in the US and in Europe.
The US is kind of dominated, isn't it, by some of the tech companies and the big supermarkets.
So there is like this middle tier, which I think is a huge opportunity going forward for this company in particular.
But they are particularly strong themselves in the UK and Europe, and they have now got several large contracts in Australia as well.
So the US isn't a huge area for them, but it's definitely a huge area of growth.
And certainly we've been talking about to some other buyers that recognize that they're large, larger, sort of in the data and retail space, and that's what they're looking at with these guys.
Do you do much shopper media stuff yourself?
Are you kind of okay with that?
We do.
We've got a.
Probably a $30 million shopper media business.
We do both media placement as well as spent a lot of time on social.
Social media marketing.
Right.
So these guys have built a SaaS product, sort of manage some of that media placement as well and the monitoring of it.
I don't know whether that's.
That's something that you have got already, but.
But certainly that's really what.
That's really what caught my interest.
Right.
I've seen this product.
I mean, we were in Omnicom's offices a couple of weeks ago and I saw them do the pitch to Omnicomp, and it's an impressive piece of kit.
I really do think that what they built is something that's useful and scalable as well.
Were they shopping the business to Omnicom?
So Omnicom have been interested.
I'll be transparent.
Omnicom have paused at the moment.
They are interested in the business, but we have a process that we're running.
And to be frank with you, the Omnicom buy side process is so slow.
It is.
I mean we would be looking at an 18 month process.
I, I chuckled at you only because when we went this last time into the market, Omnicom was one of the people that we talked to.
Yeah, slow as a word.
Yeah, so.
So actually it's my guidance.
I, I've said to the client, look, these guys are obviously really interested, would be a good fit.
But they take at least 18 months from today and we're already sort of five or six months into the process.
So my advice with them was to pause and Omnicom said, yeah, do you know what?
He's 100% right.
We're going to take forever to get this deal done.
So they are there and they're interested but it's not something that I can see closing this year.
So yeah, we've just paused them and put them to one side.
But yeah, they are out pitching all the time.
They tend to work with like really big retailers and supermarkets directly as well.
So they've got a couple of big supermarkets in the UK and some in the us sorry, some in the EU and Australia as well.
So what it does give them is a big fire hose of data as well.
You know, actual customer data, what they're purchasing and stuff.
So it's quite powerful, the power partnerships that they have and that's what's helping them to build out what they're doing.
But there's several strands to their sort of products and I'm sure given that you're already in the shop of media space, that it will be a fascinating call with the founders.
So, I mean really just staying involved.
So again, complete transparency.
There are two majority founders.
One has not been involved actively in the business for about three or four years.
He's got cancer.
He's had cancer, sorry should I say.
And he's, he's looking to get out.
But the other guy who's the tech, more the tech guy and has actually led the business for, for a long time as well.
The, the John who's leaving the business, he's kind of the more flamboyant big ideas guy.
Whereas Stuart is much more the tech and the day to day and he's the delivery guy.
So Stuart is staying on alongside Matt.
So they are looking to stay in the business for a long, for a long time.
They're not looking to get out at all and very ambitious for the business and would love to be part of something Bigger.
So yeah.
So yeah, like I say, these calls really just to check that you're alive and you're the real deal.
So I mean the kind of depth of answers I can give you versus what they can is obviously, you know, two completely different things.
So really I would love to get you set up on a call with them if you're available this week.
Yeah, well, what I'd like to do to be fair, Andrew, is so I'm a little like you, you know, I'm kind of the.
Right now finding the bills.
I'm not running a day to day business actively.
Our CEO is a gentleman named Jason Rezer.
He's got somebody that runs kind of our digital marketing area, Gerard Smith, who's an executive vice president.
Those are the two guys I'd like to kind of set up a meet and kind of talk through.
One of the things that would be helpful and I'll, I'll send you their, their contact information is if you could get them ability to see the deck.
They're covered under my NDA.
Right, because your NDA, yeah, it's all the same.
I'll, I'll get one my guys.
So yeah, if you send me their.
Content, I'll send you the names because I couldn't find a way to obviously download it, which I appreciate you guys, you're trying to be, you know.
Yeah, yeah, it's got some protection materials.
So I, I get that.
And then, you know, we'll try to get something set up and try to have some dialogue to try to understand kind of, you know, if there's a fit here.
Usually I'll just be transparent with you too.
The, the way we normally structure deals, just so you know, is we'll go through some kind of a.
And we move quickly.
So we go through some kind of a initial process to get, you know, a good overview, a good understanding of the financials.
Not with a ton of depth, but just, just some perspective.
Right.

So we can kind of get some range evaluation and then we'll put together, if that's, you know, we're feeling good about where we're at, we'll put together a letter of intent which will kind of spell out some deal structure.
Normally our deal structures are such that we'll present some cash off the table to a buyer, but we're going to also probably ask somebody to take and roll over Andrew, come back in.
That's okay.
We would ask also for some kind of a rollover kind of process, you know, so they have equity in the, in the new Established business.
Yeah.
And of course, you know, that, that's a little bit of diligence on their part, but we usually survive that fairly well because quite honestly we're not that interested in buying a business.
And it could be different.
There could be certain occasions where we might be, but that really the owner's not staying involved and staying on.
We run in these businesses, we integrate them primarily back office, but you know, we're not trying to screw them up.
So our mantra is do no harm to the employees, do no harm to the customer.
Right.

Because that's all you're buying really in these businesses is you're buying, you know, client relationship, client contracts and most of the client contracts are, well, some of them are, you know, recurring revenue, you know, the cancelable, fairly short intervals.
So you know, you, you know, you really want the owners to stay involved and then, you know, just look at this business just, just cards on the table, right.
Without any, any depth of knowledge.
It's got a high concentration in a couple of, of customers.
Right.
If you look at the, the deck you sent, you know, two customers are doing half the volume.
So that concentration would make us, you know, give pause to, you know, maybe even establishing some kind of an earn out mentality, you know, through the deal.

But again, I'm getting ahead of myself because it depends on so many other variables and, and quite honestly, you know, depending where the technology is and how unique and proprietary it is, all that might lead us to different conclusions as well.
Right.
So yeah, sure.
You know, I, I certainly don't have enough to get you, but I wanted to kind of give you some grounding of kind of know how that's really.
It'S really useful, John.

And obviously we, we've given them some advice around that, what the, the structure of a deal would look like, you know, based on, on, on those types of issues and in terms of like rollover equity and staying in the business, I mean they're, they're completely keen to do that type of deal.
They want to be in some, you know, a larger business long term and grow this thing.
You know, they're very ambitious for it.
So I, so, so certainly I can, I can confirm that they're interested in that sort of thing.
So if you can, if you can share the contacts in your organization, we can get that next stage ready to roll.
If they want a meeting with them first.
Are you going to be on that meeting?
But I can set up, I probably will, yes.
You will.
Yeah.
I'll make sure they, they do a demo of the platform and everything else as well.
So it's not just a chit chat, but they can, they can actually show you through what it is.
That's okay.
Sounds good.
I, I will get back to you today with a couple names if you could kind of then get us in the process and we'll try to get calendars locked up here in the next week or two.
Perfect.
I'll bring one of my guys in on, on that email chain as well and I'll get him to sign us.
Share the IM with your guys as well.
The, the only other question I had for you, where are you in the process?
I know it's been.
You said you've been at it a little bit bit and you know, kind of where, where are they with timing and, and suit?
So we're, we're about five, six months into the process right now.
We are looking for offers over the next sort of four, four to six weeks.
I mean, we're very keen to get an offer on the table before summer because obviously things can really slow down before then.
So that's kind of what we're looking to do.
I know you said you can move pretty fast, but my experience is if, if a buyer is interested, except for Omnicom, that they will get an LOI in pretty much within a sort of two to four week period.
They just need the financial.
We've got a data room set up already, so everything's there to share.
As soon as you, you guys have met with them and everybody likes each other, that's open doors for you guys to get in there and get an LOI based on what you can see.
Okay, sounds good.
Look, I'll, I'll be back in touch with you today and I appreciate the time.
Brilliant.
All right, great to meet you, Jam.
Take care.

summary.overview: In the M&A Introductory Call for Project Mclaren, representatives from Capital A and Market Performance Group (MPG) discussed a potential acquisition in the shopper media space. Andrew Day introduced Capital A, an M&A advisory based in the UK focused on marketing services, while John Hogan provided an overview of MPG, highlighting its impressive growth from $9 million to $225 million since 2015 and its focus on beauty, healthcare, and personal care sectors. They explored a SaaS target company with strong UK/European presence and significant retailer partnerships, acknowledging interest from Omnicom but noting their lengthy acquisition process. Discussion included the leadership of the target company, with two founders aiming to join a larger organization, and MPG's typical acquisition structure, which involves cash plus equity rollover and a focus on integrating back-office functions. Plans for next steps were outlined, including the target company preparing a demo of their platform, a timeline for offers, and setting up further meetings with key executives from both Capital A and MPG. Action items were assigned to ensure progress in the acquisition process.
summary.short_summary: During the M&A Introductory Call for Project Mclaren, Andrew Day from Capital A introduced the firm, which specializes in marketing services in the UK. John Hogan from Market Performance Group (MPG) outlined MPG's significant growth from $9 million to $225 million since 2015, focusing on sectors such as beauty, healthcare, and personal care. The discussion centered on a potential SaaS target company with a strong presence in the UK and Europe, which has established retailer partnerships. Although there is interest from Omnicom, their lengthy acquisition process was noted. The leadership of the target company, comprising two founders looking to join a larger organization, was also discussed. MPG's acquisition structure typically involves cash plus equity rollover, emphasizing back-office integration. Next steps include preparing a platform demo, outlining a timeline for offers, and scheduling further meetings with key executives from both firms.
